ratio_decidendi.ratio: The consent of the family, community, or clan is not necessary for two adult individuals to enter into a wedlock. An individual's choice of a partner is a constitutionally protected right, and class or clan honour cannot smother this choice. Any infringement of this right is a constitutional violation, and any collective action by a group to compel or punish individuals for their choice is illegal and punishable under criminal law.
obiter: The human rights of a daughter, brother, sister or son are not mortgaged to the so-called or so-understood honour of the family or clan or the collective.
The act of honour killing puts the rule of law in a catastrophic crisis.
The old order has to give way to the new. Feudal perception has to melt into oblivion paving the smooth path for liberty.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found that an individual's right to choose a life partner is a fundamental right encompassed within the right to liberty under the Constitution. This individual choice cannot be suppressed, violated, or smothered by any collective claim of 'class honour' or 'family honour.' Such notions of honour are feudal, have no constitutional or legal sanction, and any act of violence or coercion committed in their name is illegal, punishable under criminal law, and constitutes a catastrophic crisis for the rule of law.
legal_tests_applied: The court weighed the individual's fundamental right to life and liberty, specifically the freedom of choice in marriage as an inherent aspect of Article 21 of the Constitution, against the social claim of 'honour' asserted by families or community groups. It found that the fundamental right is supreme and cannot be infringed upon by extra-constitutional claims of honour.
why_respondent_won: The human rights of a daughter, brother, sister or son are not mortgaged to the so-called or so-understood honour of the family or clan or the collective.

The State is duty-bound to protect the fundamental rights of its citizens; and an inherent aspect of Article 21 of the Constitution would be the freedom of choice in marriage. Such offences are resultant of the State’s incapacity or inability to protect the fundamental rights of its citizens.

The majority in the name of class or elevated honour of clan cannot call for their presence or force their appearance... The Constitution and the laws of this country do not countenance such an act and, in fact, the whole activity is illegal and punishable as offence under the criminal law.

Once the fundamental right is inherent in a person, the intolerant groups who subscribe to the view of superiority class complex or higher clan cannot scuttle the right of a person by leaning on any kind of philosophy, moral or social, or self-proclaimed elevation.
It is the obligation of the State to have an atmosphere where the citizens are in a position to enjoy their fundamental rights.
The States have a constitutional obligation to comfort and nurture the sustenance of fundamental rights of the citizens and not to allow any hostile group to create any kind of trench in them.
policy_considerations: The act of honour killing puts the rule of law in a catastrophic crisis.
The old order has to give way to the new. Feudal perception has to melt into oblivion paving the smooth path for liberty.
It is necessary to usher in an atmosphere where the fear to get into wedlock because of the threat of the collective is dispelled.

The court perceived honour crimes with distress and expressed uneasiness and anxiety to curb such social symptoms, which are a manifestation of perverse thought, egotism at its worst and inhuman brutality.

International instruments, such as the Council of Europe Convention, condemn honour killings as a serious human rights violation and reject culture, custom, religion, tradition or so-called “honour” as justification for such acts.
